newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines starts controversial Mindanao council.
newsitem.headline: Philippines starts controversial Mindanao council.

text.p: Philippine President Fidel Ramos on Wednesday established a controversial council expected to be headed by former Moslem rebel chief Nur Misuari to supervise development in 14 provinces of the southern Mindanao region.

The presidential palace said the government would use its investments "to spur economic activities" in the Mindanao provinces, an area battered by a 24-year Moslem separatist war before the signing of peace pact in early September.

Most of the provinces are dominated by Christians, some of whom oppose the so-called Southern Philippines Council for Peace and Development (SPCPD) fearing it would lead to Moslem political ascendancy in Mindanao.
Filipino Moslems regard Mindanao as their ancestral homeland although they are now outnumbered 3-1 by Christians in the area.

Misuari last month signed a peace deal with Manila ending a rebellion that killed more than 120,000 people. He took office on Monday as governor of a smaller, semi-autonomous region comprising four Moslem provinces.
Mindanao has a total of 23 provinces but only 14 fall under the jurisdiction of the council. The remaining nine have no significant Moslem populations.
Ramos has said he will appoint Misuari to head the SPCPD, which will serve as precursor to a wider autonomy area to be created in three years after a plebiscite is held.
The expanded autonomy area could include Christian provinces that may vote to join it during the plebiscite.
Manila has committed at least $1.2 billion in aid next year to develop the SPCPD area.
